questions.stem: Book keeping is best defined as the
options: analysis and interpretation of financial statements only
systematic recording of business transactions in books of account
questions.explanation: Book keeping is the recording part of accounting; interpretation and auditing come later.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a user (beneficiary) of a trader's book-keeping records?
options: A rival trader who wants to copy the business
questions.explanation: Owners, tax authorities, lenders and investors use the records. A competitor has no legitimate claim to them.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a current asset?
options: Bank loan repayable in five years
questions.explanation: Stock is held for resale and is turned into cash within a year, so it is a current asset.

questions.stem: A trader has assets worth ₦850,000 and liabilities of ₦230,000. Her capital is
questions.explanation: Capital = Assets - Liabilities = 850,000 - 230,000 = ₦620,000.

questions.stem: Goods sold to Mr Bassey on the understanding that he will pay next month is a
questions.explanation: Payment is deferred, so it is a credit transaction.

questions.stem: In a credit sale, the person who buys the goods becomes the business's
questions.explanation: A customer who owes the business money is a debtor.

questions.stem: An account kept for a supplier to whom the business owes money is a
questions.explanation: Accounts of persons and firms (debtors and creditors) are personal accounts.

questions.stem: Rent, wages and commission received accounts are classified as
questions.explanation: Nominal accounts record incomes and expenses.

questions.stem: The source document sent by a seller to a buyer showing goods supplied on credit and the amount due is the
questions.explanation: The invoice is the source document for credit sales and purchases.

questions.stem: A credit note is issued by a seller when
options: a customer returns goods or has been overcharged
goods are first sent on credit
questions.explanation: A credit note reduces the amount the customer owes; it is the source document for returns inwards.

questions.stem: The concept that treats the business as separate from its owner is the
questions.explanation: Under the entity concept, the owner's private affairs are kept out of the business books.

questions.stem: Valuing stock at the lower of cost and net realisable value follows the convention of
questions.explanation: Prudence avoids overstating assets and profits: losses are provided for, gains are not anticipated.

questions.stem: Expenses of a year are matched against the revenue of the same year, whether or not cash has been paid. This is the
questions.explanation: The accruals concept records incomes and expenses in the period they relate to.

questions.stem: Credit sales of goods are first recorded in the
questions.explanation: The sales day book (sales journal) lists credit sales from copies of invoices.

questions.stem: The purchase of office furniture on credit is first recorded in the
questions.explanation: The purchases day book is for goods bought for resale. Fixed assets bought on credit go through the journal proper.

questions.stem: Goods returned by a customer are first entered in the
questions.explanation: Returns from customers are returns inwards (sales returns).

questions.stem: The book in which all the accounts of a business are kept is the
questions.explanation: The ledger is the main book of account containing all the individual accounts.

questions.stem: The ledger that contains the accounts of customers who buy on credit is the
questions.explanation: Customers' personal accounts are kept in the sales ledger.

questions.stem: Under the double entry principle, every transaction has
options: a debit entry and an equal credit entry
questions.explanation: Each transaction affects two accounts: one debited and one credited with the same amount.

questions.stem: Cash sales of ₦45,000 are recorded by
options: debiting Cash account and crediting Sales account
debiting Sales account and crediting Cash account
debiting Cash account and crediting Capital account
debiting Purchases account and crediting Cash account
questions.explanation: Cash comes in (debit Cash); sales income is credited.

questions.stem: The owner takes goods costing ₦12,000 from the shop for family use. The correct double entry is
questions.explanation: Goods taken by the owner reduce purchases and increase drawings.

questions.stem: A cash book with columns for cash, bank and discount is called a
questions.explanation: The three-column cash book has discount, cash and bank columns on each side.

questions.stem: When cash is taken from the office and paid into the bank, the entry in the cash book is a
questions.explanation: Both sides of the transaction appear in the cash book (Cash credit, Bank debit), shown with a "C".

questions.stem: A petty cashier is given a float of ₦20,000 under the imprest system. She spends ₦13,750 during the week. How much will she receive to restore the float?
questions.explanation: Under the imprest system, the amount spent is reimbursed, bringing the float back to ₦20,000.

questions.stem: A bank reconciliation statement is prepared to
options: explain the difference between the cash book bank balance and the bank statement balance
questions.explanation: It reconciles the two balances by identifying items not yet recorded in one or the other.

questions.stem: A cheque sent to a supplier that has not yet been paid by the bank is called
questions.explanation: It is entered in the cash book but not yet on the bank statement.

questions.stem: The cash book shows a bank balance of ₦145,000. Unpresented cheques amount to ₦30,000 and uncredited lodgements to ₦18,000. The balance on the bank statement should be
questions.explanation: 145,000 + 30,000 (not yet deducted by bank) - 18,000 (not yet added by bank) = ₦157,000.

questions.stem: A trial balance is a list of
options: all invoices sent out in a year
ledger balances on a particular date
questions.explanation: It lists all debit and credit balances to check arithmetical accuracy.

questions.stem: Which of these errors will NOT be revealed by a trial balance?
options: Error in adding the sales account
Entering a debit on the debit side twice
questions.explanation: If a transaction is completely omitted, both sides are left out equally, so the trial balance still agrees.

questions.stem: Repairs to a motor van were wrongly debited to the Motor Van account. This is an error of
questions.explanation: A revenue expense was posted to a capital (asset) account, which is an error of principle.

questions.stem: The trading account is prepared to find the
questions.explanation: Trading account compares sales with cost of sales to give gross profit.

questions.stem: Opening stock ₦40,000; purchases ₦260,000; closing stock ₦55,000; sales ₦380,000. The gross profit is
Under the FIFO method of stock valuation, closing stock is valued at
questions.explanation: FIFO assumes the earliest goods are sold first, so the goods left are from the latest purchases.

questions.stem: Which of these items is debited to the Profit and Loss Account?
questions.explanation: Expenses such as salaries are debited; incomes are credited.

questions.stem: Gross profit ₦135,000; discount received ₦5,000; rent ₦30,000; salaries ₦45,000. The net profit is
Carriage outwards is treated as
options: an expense in the Profit and Loss Account
part of cost of sales in the Trading Account
questions.explanation: Carriage outwards is a selling and distribution expense, so it goes to the P&L. Carriage inwards goes to the trading account.

questions.stem: A balance sheet shows the
options: financial position of a business at a particular date
cash received and paid in a month
questions.explanation: The balance sheet lists assets, liabilities and capital at one date.

questions.stem: Capital at start ₦500,000; net profit ₦120,000; drawings ₦40,000. Closing capital in the balance sheet is
Working capital is calculated as
questions.explanation: Working capital (net current assets) = current assets - current liabilities.

questions.topic: Adjustments for prepayments, accruals, depreciation, bad and doubtful debts
questions.stem: Rent payable is ₦72,000 a year, but ₦90,000 was paid during the year. The rent charged to the Profit and Loss Account is
questions.explanation: Only the year's rent is charged; the extra ₦18,000 is a prepayment (current asset).

questions.topic: Adjustments for prepayments, accruals, depreciation, bad and doubtful debts
questions.stem: Wages paid during the year were ₦140,000 and ₦15,000 was still owing at the year end. The wages charged to the P&L is
questions.explanation: Accrued wages are added: 140,000 + 15,000 = ₦155,000.

questions.topic: Adjustments for prepayments, accruals, depreciation, bad and doubtful debts
questions.stem: Debtors are ₦200,000 before writing off bad debts of ₦8,000. A provision for doubtful debts of 5% is to be created. The provision is
Depreciation is the
options: increase in value of an asset
loss in value of a fixed asset over its useful life
questions.explanation: Fixed assets lose value through use, wear and tear and age.

questions.stem: A machine cost ₦1,200,000 and is expected to last 5 years with a scrap value of ₦200,000. Using the straight line method, annual depreciation is
A van costing ₦500,000 is depreciated at 20% per annum on the reducing balance method. The depreciation for the SECOND year is
Which of these items appears on the CREDIT side of a Sales Ledger Control Account?
questions.explanation: Items that reduce debtors (cash received, discounts allowed, returns inwards, bad debts) are credited.

questions.stem: Opening debtors ₦60,000; credit sales ₦240,000; cash received from debtors ₦210,000; discounts allowed ₦4,000; returns inwards ₦6,000. Closing debtors are
A Purchases Ledger Control Account is also called a
questions.explanation: It summarises all creditors' accounts in the purchases ledger.

questions.stem: A system in which a trader keeps only a cash book and personal accounts is called
questions.explanation: Single entry records are incomplete because each transaction is not recorded twice.

questions.stem: A main limitation of single entry is that
options: a trial balance cannot be extracted to check accuracy
it is too expensive for small traders
questions.explanation: Without double entry there is no trial balance and errors are hard to detect.

questions.stem: Opening capital ₦300,000; closing capital ₦380,000; drawings ₦50,000; additional capital introduced ₦20,000. The net profit is
The account of a club that summarises all cash received and paid during a year is the
questions.explanation: It is a summary of the cash book.

questions.stem: In a not-for-profit organisation, the excess of assets over liabilities is called
questions.explanation: Accumulated fund takes the place of capital in a club's accounts.

questions.stem: A club received ₦85,000 in subscriptions during the year, of which ₦5,000 was for next year. Subscriptions of ₦7,000 for the current year were still owing. The subscription income for the year is
Direct materials plus direct labour plus direct expenses gives
questions.explanation: Prime cost is the total of direct costs.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a factory overhead?
questions.explanation: Supervisors are indirect labour, so their salary is a factory overhead.

questions.stem: Prime cost ₦240,000; factory overheads ₦60,000; opening work in progress ₦15,000; closing work in progress ₦25,000. The cost of production is
The written agreement that sets out how a partnership will be run is the
questions.explanation: The deed covers capital, profit sharing, salaries and interest.

questions.stem: In the absence of a partnership agreement, profits and losses are shared
options: in the ratio of time worked
questions.explanation: The Partnership Act provides equal sharing where there is no agreement.

questions.stem: Ada and Bayo share profits 3:2 after interest on capital and Bayo's salary of ₦30,000. Net profit is ₦240,000 and interest on capital is ₦40,000 for Ada and ₦20,000 for Bayo. Bayo's share of the remaining profit is
A joint venture is
options: a temporary partnership formed for a particular business project
a permanent company owned by shareholders
questions.explanation: A joint venture ends when the venture is completed.

questions.stem: One difference between a joint venture and a partnership is that a joint venture
options: ends when the particular project is completed
is a legal entity separate from its members
questions.explanation: A partnership is a continuing business; a joint venture is for one project.

questions.stem: Rent of ₦120,000 is to be shared between Departments A and B on the basis of floor area of 300 m² and 200 m². Department A bears
The main purpose of departmental accounts is to
options: show the profit or loss made by each section of the business
questions.explanation: They show which departments are profitable.

questions.stem: The owners of a limited liability company are called
questions.explanation: Shareholders own the company; directors manage it.

questions.stem: A company has issued 500,000 ordinary shares of ₦1 each and declares a dividend of 10%. The total dividend is
Shareholders who receive a fixed rate of dividend before ordinary shareholders are paid hold
questions.explanation: Preference shares carry a fixed dividend paid before ordinary dividends. Debentures are loans and earn interest.

questions.stem: Sales ₦400,000 and gross profit ₦120,000. The gross profit margin is
Current assets ₦180,000 (including stock ₦60,000) and current liabilities ₦60,000. The quick (acid test) ratio is
Cost of sales ₦280,000; opening stock ₦30,000; closing stock ₦40,000. The rate of stock turnover is
A business with assets of ₦1,050,000 and liabilities of ₦250,000 is bought for ₦900,000. The goodwill is
The amount agreed to be paid for a business that is taken over is called the
questions.explanation: Purchase consideration is the price paid for the business.

questions.stem: In a consignment, the person who sends the goods to be sold is the
questions.explanation: The consignor owns the goods; the consignee sells them on his behalf.

questions.stem: The statement sent by the consignee to the consignor showing sales, expenses and commission is the
questions.explanation: The account sales reports the results of the consignment.

questions.stem: A machine has a cash price of ₦600,000. Under hire purchase, a deposit of ₦150,000 is paid followed by four instalments of ₦125,000. The total interest is
Under hire purchase, ownership of the goods passes to the hirer
options: when the last instalment is paid
questions.explanation: The seller remains owner until all instalments are paid.

questions.stem: In contract accounts, the amount kept back by the customer from the value of work certified until the work is proved satisfactory is
questions.explanation: Retention protects the customer against defects.

questions.stem: Notional profit ₦90,000; work certified ₦600,000; cash received ₦480,000. Using 2/3 x notional profit x cash received / work certified, the profit taken to P&L is
A cooperative society is mainly formed to
options: promote the welfare of its members rather than to maximise profit
make the highest possible profit for outside shareholders
questions.explanation: Cooperatives serve their members' economic needs.

questions.stem: In a consumer cooperative, surplus is often shared among members according to
options: the number of shares sold to the public
the value of their purchases from the society
questions.explanation: This patronage dividend rewards members in proportion to their dealings with the society.

questions.stem:
(a) Distinguish between an accounting concept and an accounting convention. [2 marks]
(b) Explain the following: (i) going concern concept; (ii) consistency convention; (iii) materiality convention; (iv) money measurement concept. [8 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) a concept is a basic assumption underlying accounts; a convention is a generally accepted practice or custom in applying the concepts
2 marks: (b)(i) the business is assumed to continue in operation for the foreseeable future, so assets are valued at cost, not break-up value
2 marks: (b)(ii) the same accounting methods should be used from year to year so that results can be compared
2 marks: (b)(iii) items too small to affect decisions may be treated in the simplest way, e.g. a stapler expensed
2 marks: (b)(iv) only items that can be expressed in money are recorded
questions.explanation: Concepts are basic assumptions; conventions are customary practices. Going concern assumes the business will continue; consistency requires the same methods each year; materiality allows small items to be treated simply; money measurement records only what can be valued in money.

questions.stem:
(a) Explain the meaning of source documents. [2 marks]
(b) Name the source document and the book of original entry for each of the following transactions:
(i) goods sold on credit to Amaka; (ii) goods returned to Musa, a supplier; (iii) cash received from a customer; (iv) small payment for cleaning materials. [8 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) the original documents that provide evidence of transactions and from which entries are made in the books
2 marks: (b)(i) invoice (copy) - sales day book
2 marks: (b)(ii) debit note (or credit note received) - returns outwards book
2 marks: (b)(iii) receipt (copy) - cash book
2 marks: (b)(iv) petty cash voucher - petty cash book
questions.explanation: Source documents are the original evidence of transactions. Credit sales: invoice, sales day book. Returns to supplier: debit note, returns outwards book. Cash received: receipt, cash book. Small payment: petty cash voucher, petty cash book.

questions.stem:
(a) State three functions of a trial balance. [3 marks]
(b) Explain, with an example, each of the following errors that do not affect the agreement of a trial balance: (i) error of commission; (ii) compensating error; (iii) error of complete reversal. [6 marks]
(c) What is a suspense account? [1 mark]
questions.markingGuide:
3 marks: (a) any three: checks arithmetical accuracy of the ledger; provides a summary of balances; helps in preparing final accounts; helps detect some errors (1 mark each)
2 marks: (b)(i) correct amount posted to the correct side of the wrong account of the same class, e.g. sale to A. Musa posted to M. Musa's account
2 marks: (b)(ii) two errors of equal amount on opposite sides cancel out, e.g. sales overcast by ₦1,000 and rent overcast by ₦1,000
2 marks: (b)(iii) the correct accounts are used but the debit and credit are reversed, e.g. cash paid to supplier debited to Cash and credited to supplier
1 mark: (c) a temporary account opened to make the trial balance agree until errors are found and corrected
questions.explanation: A trial balance checks arithmetical accuracy and helps prepare final accounts. Error of commission: right class, wrong account. Compensating: equal errors cancel. Complete reversal: debit and credit swapped. A suspense account temporarily holds a trial balance difference.

questions.stem:
(a) Explain the meaning of a joint venture. [2 marks]
(b) State four differences between a joint venture and a partnership. [8 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) a temporary business arrangement in which two or more persons combine to carry out a particular project and share the profit or loss
8 marks: (b) any four, 2 marks each: JV is temporary, partnership is continuing; JV has no firm name, partnership has; JV books may be kept by each venturer, partnership keeps one set; JV ends on completion of project, partnership continues until dissolved; JV profit shared once at the end, partnership profit shared periodically; JV need not be registered
questions.explanation: A joint venture is a temporary association for a specific project. Unlike a partnership, it has no firm name, ends on completion of the venture, shares profit at the end, and may not keep a single set of books.

questions.stem:
Ngozi Stores had the following transactions in March:
Mar 1 Cash in hand ₦25,000; cash at bank ₦180,000
Mar 4 Cash sales ₦38,000
Mar 8 Paid Emeka by cheque ₦47,500 after deducting discount of ₦2,500
Mar 12 Received a cheque from Tolu ₦57,000 in full settlement of a debt of ₦60,000; paid into bank
Mar 18 Paid ₦40,000 cash into the bank
Mar 25 Paid wages in cash ₦15,000
Mar 30 Withdrew ₦20,000 from the bank for office use
Prepare a three-column cash book and balance it on 31 March. [20 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: correct headings with Discount, Cash and Bank columns on both sides
2 marks: opening balances cash ₦25,000 and bank ₦180,000 on the debit side
2 marks: cash sales ₦38,000 debit cash
3 marks: Emeka: bank credit ₦47,500 and discount received ₦2,500 on credit side
3 marks: Tolu: bank debit ₦57,000 and discount allowed ₦3,000 on debit side
2 marks: contra Mar 18: cash credit ₦40,000 and bank debit ₦40,000 marked C
1 mark: wages cash credit ₦15,000
2 marks: contra Mar 30: bank credit ₦20,000 and cash debit ₦20,000 marked C
2 marks: closing balances c/d: cash ₦28,000 and bank ₦209,500
1 mark: discount totals: allowed ₦3,000, received ₦2,500
questions.explanation: Cash: 25,000 + 38,000 + 20,000 = 83,000 in; 40,000 + 15,000 out; balance ₦28,000. Bank: 180,000 + 57,000 + 40,000 = 277,000 in; 47,500 + 20,000 out; balance ₦209,500. Discount allowed ₦3,000 (debit side), discount received ₦2,500 (credit side).

questions.stem:
On 31 May, the cash book of Ibe Ventures showed a debit bank balance of ₦212,000, but the bank statement on that date showed a different balance. Investigation revealed:
(i) Cheques of ₦46,000 issued to suppliers had not been presented for payment.
(ii) A cheque of ₦30,000 paid into the bank on 31 May had not yet been credited.
(iii) Bank charges of ₦2,500 appeared only on the bank statement.
(iv) A customer paid ₦18,000 directly into the bank account; this was not in the cash book.
(v) A dividend of ₦9,500 was received by the bank on behalf of Ibe Ventures but not entered in the cash book.
(a) Prepare the adjusted cash book (bank column). [8 marks]
(b) Prepare a bank reconciliation statement as at 31 May. [8 marks]
(c) State two reasons for preparing a bank reconciliation statement. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) balance b/d ₦212,000 debit
2 marks: (a) debit direct credit ₦18,000 and dividend ₦9,500
2 marks: (a) credit bank charges ₦2,500
2 marks: (a) adjusted balance ₦237,000
2 marks: (b) start with adjusted cash book balance ₦237,000
2 marks: (b) add unpresented cheques ₦46,000
2 marks: (b) less uncredited lodgement ₦30,000
2 marks: (b) balance as per bank statement ₦253,000
4 marks: (c) any two: to detect errors; to update the cash book; to detect fraud; to explain the difference between the two balances (2 marks each)
questions.explanation: Adjusted cash book: 212,000 + 18,000 + 9,500 - 2,500 = ₦237,000. Reconciliation: 237,000 + 46,000 - 30,000 = ₦253,000 per bank statement. It is prepared to find errors and omissions, update the cash book and deter fraud.

questions.stem:
The following balances were extracted from the books of Halima Abubakar, a sole trader, on 31 December:
Sales ₦920,000; Purchases ₦610,000; Stock 1 January ₦85,000; Returns inwards ₦20,000; Returns outwards ₦15,000; Carriage inwards ₦12,000; Carriage outwards ₦9,000; Salaries ₦96,000; Rent ₦60,000; Discount received ₦6,000; General expenses ₦24,000.
Stock on 31 December was valued at ₦98,000.
Prepare the Trading and Profit and Loss Account for the year ended 31 December. [20 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: net sales 920,000 - 20,000 = ₦900,000
2 marks: net purchases 610,000 - 15,000 = ₦595,000
2 marks: carriage inwards ₦12,000 added to purchases
2 marks: opening stock ₦85,000 added
2 marks: closing stock ₦98,000 deducted
2 marks: cost of sales ₦594,000
2 marks: gross profit ₦306,000
1 mark: discount received ₦6,000 added to gross profit
3 marks: expenses: carriage outwards 9,000, salaries 96,000, rent 60,000, general expenses 24,000 = ₦189,000
2 marks: net profit ₦123,000

questions.topic: Adjustments for prepayments, accruals, depreciation, bad and doubtful debts
questions.stem:
Tunde's trial balance at 31 December shows: Debtors ₦250,000; Provision for doubtful debts (1 January) ₦8,000; Rent ₦66,000; Insurance ₦24,000; Wages ₦180,000; Motor vehicle at cost ₦800,000.
Additional information:
(i) Bad debts of ₦10,000 are to be written off.
(ii) Provision for doubtful debts is to be 5% of the remaining debtors.
(iii) Rent of ₦6,000 is owing.
(iv) Insurance of ₦4,000 is prepaid.
(v) Wages accrued ₦12,000.
(vi) Depreciate the motor vehicle at 15% per annum on cost.
Calculate the amount for each item to appear in the Profit and Loss Account and show how debtors, the motor vehicle, the prepayment and the accruals appear in the balance sheet. [20 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: bad debts ₦10,000 in P&L
2 marks: new provision 5% x 240,000 = ₦12,000; increase in provision ₦4,000 charged to P&L
2 marks: rent charged ₦72,000
2 marks: insurance charged ₦20,000
2 marks: wages charged ₦192,000
2 marks: depreciation ₦120,000
2 marks: balance sheet debtors 240,000 less provision 12,000 = ₦228,000
2 marks: motor vehicle 800,000 less depreciation 120,000 = ₦680,000
2 marks: prepaid insurance ₦4,000 as a current asset
2 marks: accruals: rent ₦6,000 and wages ₦12,000 (total ₦18,000) as current liabilities
questions.explanation: P&L: bad debts 10,000; increase in provision 4,000 (12,000 - 8,000); rent 72,000; insurance 20,000; wages 192,000; depreciation 120,000. Balance sheet: debtors 228,000 net; motor vehicle 680,000 NBV; prepayment 4,000; accruals 18,000.

questions.stem:
Ada and Bayo are partners sharing profits and losses in the ratio 3:2. Their capitals are Ada ₦400,000 and Bayo ₦200,000. The partnership agreement provides for:
(i) interest on capital at 10% per annum;
(ii) a salary of ₦30,000 a year for Bayo;
(iii) interest on drawings: Ada ₦3,000, Bayo ₦2,000.
Net profit for the year was ₦240,000. Drawings were Ada ₦50,000 and Bayo ₦40,000. Current account balances at the start of the year were Ada ₦10,000 (credit) and Bayo ₦5,000 (credit).
(a) Prepare the Profit and Loss Appropriation Account. [10 marks]
(b) Prepare the partners' current accounts. [10 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: (a) net profit ₦240,000
1 mark: (a) add interest on drawings ₦5,000 (Ada 3,000, Bayo 2,000)
2 marks: (a) interest on capital: Ada ₦40,000, Bayo ₦20,000
2 marks: (a) salary Bayo ₦30,000
2 marks: (a) residual profit ₦155,000
2 marks: (a) shared Ada ₦93,000, Bayo ₦62,000
2 marks: (b) credit balances b/d Ada 10,000, Bayo 5,000
2 marks: (b) credits for interest on capital, salary and share of profit

questions.stem:
The following is a summary of the cash book of Unity Youth Club for the year ended 31 December:
Receipts: Balance b/f ₦45,000; Subscriptions ₦160,000; Proceeds of dance ₦70,000; General donations ₦25,000.
Payments: Rent of hall ₦48,000; Dance expenses ₦30,000; Purchase of chairs ₦80,000; Secretary's honorarium ₦36,000; Stationery ₦9,000.
Additional information: subscriptions owing at 31 December were ₦12,000; rent of ₦4,000 was prepaid at 31 December.
(a) Prepare the Receipts and Payments Account. [8 marks]
(b) Prepare the Income and Expenditure Account for the year. [12 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) receipts total ₦300,000 including balance b/f
2 marks: (a) payments listed totalling ₦203,000
2 marks: (a) balance c/d ₦97,000
2 marks: (a) correct format
2 marks: (b) subscriptions 160,000 + 12,000 = ₦172,000
2 marks: (b) profit on dance 70,000 - 30,000 = ₦40,000
2 marks: (b) general donations ₦25,000 as income
2 marks: (b) rent 48,000 - 4,000 = ₦44,000
2 marks: (b) honorarium ₦36,000 and stationery ₦9,000; chairs excluded as capital expenditure
2 marks: (b) surplus of income over expenditure ₦148,000
questions.explanation: Receipts and Payments: total receipts 300,000; payments 203,000; balance c/d ₦97,000. I&E: income 172,000 + 40,000 + 25,000 = 237,000; expenditure 44,000 + 36,000 + 9,000 = 89,000; surplus ₦148,000. Chairs are capital items for the balance sheet.
